standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label remark-extend-to-finite-locally-free, invoked at proof line 9114
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes what c of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules is supposed to mean, so that independence of the representing complex is a well posed question.

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of the bivariant theory over an open and closed decomposition, and vanishing of a bivariant class
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-disjoint-decomposition-bivariant (proof line 9131) and lemma-bivariant-zero (proof line 9141)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives A^p(X) as the product of the A^p(X_i) so that the components can be glued, and reduces equality of bivariant classes to equality after capping with [Y] for every integral Y.

standard_prerequisites.name: Tor dimension at most one after a proper birational modification, and Schanuel's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Flatness, labels flat-lemma-blowup-complex-integral (proof line 9148) and flat-remark-when-you-have-a-complex (proof line 9163); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-Schanuel (proof line 9203)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces to complexes of constant rank whose cohomology has tor dimension at most one, in which case kernels and images are finite locally free, and identifies the two kernels in the final four-term diagram chase.

core_obligations: Decompose X into open and closed subschemes X_i on which all the ranks of the complex are constant, use local boundedness so that only finitely many terms are nonzero on each X_i, define c on each X_i by the alternating product of the total Chern classes, and glue the components using A^p(X) = product_i A^p(X_i) (proof lines 9113-9134).

Reduce the comparison of two representing complexes E^bullet and F^bullet to an integral base: for g : Y -> X locally of finite type with Y integral, it suffices by the bivariant vanishing criterion to compare c(g^*E^bullet) cap [Y] with c(g^*F^bullet) cap [Y], and one may replace Y by a proper birational integral cover (proof lines 9137-9145).

Further reduce to bounded complexes of constant rank whose cohomology sheaves are perfect of tor dimension at most one, where kernels and images are finite locally free; rewrite both total Chern classes as alternating products over kernels and images and use the two short exact sequences with common quotient H^i(E) to reduce to the final comparison (proof lines 9147-9179).

Settle the reduced problem: for short exact sequences 0 -> E' -> E -> Q -> 0 and 0 -> F' -> F -> Q -> 0 with E, E', F, F' finite locally free and Q of tor dimension at most one, form G as the kernel of E direct sum F -> Q, note G is finite locally free, do the diagram chase identifying its two subkernels with E' and F' up to the two surjections, and conclude c(E)c(F') = c(G) = c(F)c(E') (proof lines 9181-9209).
proof_roadmap: Glue the local definition of the total Chern class of the complex from its rank-constant pieces (proof lines 9113-9134).
Reduce the comparison of two representing complexes to an integral Y, then to a proper birational cover on which the cohomology has tor dimension at most one (proof lines 9137-9151).
Rewrite the class through kernels and images, then finish with the standard Schanuel-style computation in the four-term diagram (proof lines 9153-9209).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that three invariants of a perfect object E in D(O_X) defined by choosing a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, namely the total Chern class, the Chern character and the Chern polynomials, do not depend on the choice of complex (statement lines 9090-9104, tag 0ESZ). The proof is a genuine three-stage reduction rather than a citation: it first glues the construction over a rank-constant open and closed decomposition, then uses a bivariant vanishing criterion to move to a proper birational integral cover on which the cohomology acquires tor dimension at most one, and finally analyses the resulting four-term diagram with Schanuel's lemma to compare two short exact sequences with a common quotient. The bookkeeping is delicate but each step is standard, so the claim is H2.
